Company size and individual executive actions together influence Responsible AI (RAI) prioritization in several ways. Larger companies may have more resources to invest in RAI initiatives and can afford to offer training sessions to existing employees about RAI topics. They often aim to retain employees for a long time, which can lead to a more stable culture around RAI. In contrast, smaller companies may have a more unified leadership that can quickly implement RAI priorities if an executive is motivated to champion these efforts.

Individual executive actions can significantly impact RAI prioritization, especially when executives have sufficient power or when the company is hierarchical. For instance, if an executive is inspired by an event or conference, they may push for RAI initiatives. However, individual circumstances can also lead to deprioritization of RAI if executives fear setting precedents or if previous RAI efforts did not yield positive results. Thus, the interplay between company size and the actions of individual executives creates a complex landscape for RAI prioritization, where larger organizations may have the capacity for RAI but also face more bureaucratic challenges, while smaller organizations may be more agile but dependent on the motivation of key individuals.
